item.title: With nine new recordings of Mahler’s epic Resurrection Symphony this year alone, which rises above the rest?
item.description: The second – the ‘Resurrection’ – was the first Mahler symphony ever to be recorded, and it is still today an essential work in any conductor’s catalogue. Or is it simply that triumph over adversity sells in today’s uncertain world? item.title: ‘They were brilliant people’: fascinating film reveals a Harlem Renaissance reunion
item.description: In the dazzling archival documentary Once Upon a Time in Harlem, a 1972 cocktail party brings together various creative luminaries as they discuss and debate More than a flowering of the arts at the dawn of the 20th century, the Harlem Renaissance marked the breakthrough moment when Black Americans asserted their creative control, defining a culture that had been purpose-built to exclude them. item.title: ‘Capturing Bigfoot’ Review: An Astounding Documentary Uncovers the Truth
item.description: "Capturing Bigfoot" is an amazing documentary about the legend of Bigfoot — about how it was born, how it took hold, and how that iconic piece of film footage came to be. It’s a documentary that answers all the questions and solves all the mysteries. Unlike your typical film about UFOs, it doesn’t leave you with that vague feeling of "The truth is still out there, and I’m not sure what it is." "Capturing Bigfoot" shows you the truth, but what it really shows you is what that truth says about us, a society that went down the rabbit hole of wanting to believe and now, increasingly, lives there. Fuente: Variety.

item.title: El Chernóbil asturiano: el pueblo abandonado ubicado junto a una antigua central térmica que tiene cine, escuela, club social y hasta consultorio médico
item.description: Había una vez un pueblo con cine, escuela, club social, piscina y hasta un consultorio médico de rigor. Solo que está abandonado. No es un cuento, existe, está en Tineo (Asturias) y se llama Soto de la Barca. Algunos apodan a este lugar el “Chernóbil asturiano”, aunque aquí nunca hubo un reactor nuclear. Prípiat tuvos plazos y 49.000 evacuados. Soto no recibió ni la alerta de la sirena: se vació a cámara lenta, nómina a nómina.
